title: True a wobbly bicycle wheel
instruction: Adjust the spoke nipples to leave the bicycle wheel running straight and freely rotating.
context: Bicycle mechanics correct a wheel by finding the wobble and redistributing spoke tension without making the wheel loose or off-centre.
setup: Proposed fixed setup in setup.json: a 420 mm aluminium rim with 32 steel 2 mm spokes and 12 mm brass nipples, mounted upright in a single-sided steel truing stand. Two adjacent same-side nipples start 0.75 turn loose. A free 243 mm steel spoke key has a 3.25 mm slot, a 175 mm neck and a 55 mm grip. The candidate robot layout clocks the wheel by 50° and phases its square flats by 45°. Exact geometry and coordinates are listed; a complete native robot repair and final setup screenshot remain unvalidated.
scoring: 0.5 for at most 1.5 mm peak-to-peak lateral runout; 1.0 for at most 0.5 mm. Both require a complete released revolution, radial runout at most 1 mm, dish error at most 0.5 mm, and every spoke within the specified fixture tension range of 400–1000 N. Check tension with a mechanical spoke tensiometer and its steel/2 mm conversion chart. Damage, direct rim bending, external bracing, invalid evidence or any other outcome scores zero. Proposed limits await stable full-scene verification.
run_limit: Proposed 3,600 control steps (180 seconds at 20 Hz); no robot run yet.
reset_notes: Restore the same documented nipple rest lengths and intact wheel. Initial wobble is created by uneven spoke rest lengths, not a bent rim animation.
fidelity: Native compliant rim joints, tension-only bending spokes and physically rotating square nipples. Measured nipple rotation relative to its spoke changes thread rest length and produces equal and opposite torque. A contact-driven wrench fixture transfers 32.90° of a 45° command with valid rim integrity. The YAM CPU bridge completes short checks; GPU YAM shows unexplained wheel acceleration and is unsuitable. A full robot repair has not yet been demonstrated. Thread friction and elastic material limits are disclosed engineering approximations.
scores: Not run. No demo, Dream score or media exists. This is not submission metadata.
